title: Ang 1118–1124: Kedara
tomorrow: after an evening raga, what does the morning sing first?

cards: The porch at the end of a long day. Shoes off, the street going quiet, the sky turning the color of chai. That's the hour this week lands in.
A grandmother's couplet at the door: when You are on my side. A warrior who never leaves the field. A canopy over the one the world shunned.
A raga of courage, walked end to end. A year of months, each one a letter. A long night kept as a watch.
Six days. And now Kedara, a short raga that tradition gives to the evening.

teach.h: RAM DAS: SING IT EVERY DAY.
teach.b: Kedara opens on ang 1118 with Guru Ram Das, the fourth Guru, and his first line is, in paraphrase: O my mind, sing the Name of the Lord, every day. Not once, after a big moment. Every day, including the ordinary ones.
Then, near the end, two Bhagats.
Kabir, on ang 1123, in paraphrase: let go of both praise and slander, give up pride.
Ravidas, on ang 1124: a family full of rituals means little if devotion isn't in the heart. Put the three together and you get an evening checklist. Let the day's compliments and insults both go.
Don't lean on where you come from. Sing the Name, and come back tomorrow. That's what's left to sing when the day is done.
Not a scoreboard of who praised you and who didn't, but a refrain you can pick up again in the morning.

how: Hymns in raga Kedara are sung in kirtan and read in order in a complete reading of the Guru Granth Sahib.

s: Kabir in Kedara says to enjoy praise and ignore only the insults
let go of both praise and slander, and of pride (ang 1123).
Guru Ram Das opens Kedara asking the mind to sing the Name every day
not once after a big moment: every day.
Ravidas says a family of rituals is enough on its own
it means little if devotion isn't in the heart (ang 1124).

games.q: your project gets loud praise at work today, and one sharp comment. it's evening. what would Kedara's checklist suggest?
o: let both go, and come back tomorrow to the steady refrain.
replay the praise so the sharp comment can't stick.
replay the sharp comment until you've fixed every flaw.
games.why: Kabir: let go of both praise and slander. Ram Das: sing the Name every day. evening isn't a scoreboard.

practice: Look toward the nearest window or the softest light in the room, and just watch it for the whole sit. Let one compliment from this week go, and one sting too, as the light settles.
